title: Crossfade bridge notes: midnight-to-dawn handoff
content:
Summary:
- Shift window: 2027-12-07 00:00 - 2027-12-07 08:00 PST (this doc created at 00:30).
- Purpose: handoff for cross-region latency spike on embedding endpoints and follow-up tasks for next shift.

Key status:
- Customer-impacting: No active customer-visible errors now. 95th/99th tail latency for /v1/embeddings returned to baseline by 00:10 after mitigation.
- Services involved: embedding-service (primary), kv-cache (prefix cache layer), model-router.
- Severity: Sev2 (brief spike degrading throughput, transient 2–5min bursts).
- Current state: Stable. Active monitoring: embedding-service p99 < 800ms last 30m.

Incident TL;DR (what happened):
- 23:47 PST: Alerting spike: embedding p99 jumped to ~3s from baseline ~500ms for ~3m rolling windows.
- 23:48 PST: Automatic fallback to model-variant-b triggered for a subset of requests; error rates stayed low but latency remained high.
- 23:50 PST: SRE on-call (me) began triage. Observed simultaneous increase in cache eviction rates on kv-cache nodes in us-west-2 + unusual thundering herd on certain prefixes.
- 23:52 PST: Manually increased kv-cache connection count and temporarily disabled aggressive prefix eviction policy (see runbook step 4 override).
- 00:02 PST: Latency trend returned to acceptable range; model-router fallback metrics normalized.

Timeline (brief):
- 23:46:27 Alert: embedding-service.p99 > 2000ms - automated paging.
- 23:47:10 Slack thread #infra-ops: "embedding p99 rising — investigating". Priya joined.
- 23:48:02 Observed kv-cache eviction spike (metric: kv_cache.evictions_per_min ↑ 6x).
- 23:49:15 Confirmed correlation between eviction bursts and embedding tail latency.
- 23:50:30 Applied temporary config: kv-cache.eviction_threshold -> +20%.
- 23:51:40 Started synthetic check ramp to validate model-router fallbacks.
- 00:01:55 Metrics show p99 trend back near baseline.
- 00:10:00 Closed incident slack thread, set post-incident task list.

What likely caused it:
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden workload spike targeting a small set of cold prefixes caused eviction churn in kv-cache, which increased first-token latency for model calls and triggered downstream slow paths in the serving runtime.
- Contributing factors: eviction policy tuned too aggressively for memory pressure assumptions; no adaptive ramp for sudden prefix-heavy workloads; model-router fallback threshold too sensitive to short-lived tail spikes.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Temporarily raised eviction threshold on affected kv-cache pool (us-west-2) — manual override.
- Bumped kv-cache connection pool sizes on two nodes to smooth throughput.
- Added a short-lived traffic-shaping rate limit for high-QPS client tokens (rule id: svc-temp-rt-77) to reduce overload on cold-prefix hot spots.

Testing & verification performed:
- Runbook synthetic tests executed (cache-hit, cold-prefix replay) — passed 3/3 scenarios post-mitigation.
- Canary traffic showed stable latencies for 20m following change.
- No increase in 5xx errors observed in the window.

Open follow-ups (assigned):
- SRE-001: Update kv-cache runbook to add a 'sudden-prefix-burst' play with step-by-step threshold adjustments and safe rollback commands. Owner: Priya Malhotra. Due: 2027-12-09.
- SRE-002: Tune model-router fallback window to avoid flapping on <2m tail spikes; propose new threshold values and run 24h A/B test. Owner: Diego Ramirez. Due: 2027-12-10.
- SRE-003: Create a synthetic that replays cold-prefix bursts at scale (100k req/min for 1m) and add to nightly regression suite. Owner: Evan Chen. Due: 2027-12-13.
- SRE-004: Review and increase alert debounce for embedding p99 alerts to reduce noisy pages; coordinate with monitoring team. Owner: oncall-next (see roster). Due: 2027-12-08.

Changes to runbooks / notes to incorporate:
- Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/team/sre/runbooks/cache-eviction (needs new section).
- Add 'safe knobs' that can be toggled without rolling restarts: eviction_threshold, conn_pool_size, prefix-rate-limit. Include exact CLI commands used tonight and safe-rollback commands (I put them in the linked PR: PR#1123).
- Document metrics to watch: kv_cache.evictions_per_min, embedding_service.p99, model_router.fallback_rate, tcp_conn_reuse_pct.

Monitoring & dashboards to tweak:
- Add a small panel to the embedding dashboard that correlates kv_cache.evictions_per_min with embedding_service.p99 over a 30m window (visual correlation helps quick triage).
- Add alert: if kv_cache.evictions_per_min increases by >4x and embedding_service.p99 > 1500ms for >=3m, route to SEV2 channel with runbook link.

Notes to incoming on-call (practical):
- Primary checks: embedding-service health + kv-cache pool metrics. Use the synthetic test tool (synth-check -r embeddings/cold-prefix) if any anomaly appears.
- Slack: #infra-ops (pager), thread pinned: "embedding p99 spike 2027-12-07".
- Escalation order: on-call -> priya (pager) -> eng-lead (Diego) -> paging list in Confluence.
- If you see p99 > 2s for more than 4m and kv_cache.evictions_per_min > 3x baseline, escalate immediately.

Administrative / retro items:
- Consider a short-lived memtier expansion for kv-cache pool autoscaler during high holidays (observed slightly higher traffic patterns).
- We'll add a retrospective note in the weekly SRE retro (Wed 2027-12-08) to review thresholding strategy.

Logs & artifacts (quick links):
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-7892
- Runbook edit PR: PR#1123 (contains exact commands and rollback)
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/infra-ops/p1234567890 (pinned messages)

Quick command cheatsheet used tonight (copy to runbook):
- Increase eviction threshold: infractl cache set-eviction --pool us-west-2 --pct +20
- Increase conn pool: infractl cache set-conns --pool us-west-2 --add 50
- Temporarily apply rate cap: infractl rate-limit apply --rule svc-temp-rt-77 --qps 2000 --duration 10m
- Rollback eviction threshold: infractl cache set-eviction --pool us-west-2 --pct -20

Closing note:
- No customer-facing incident page required (impact window brief and self-mitigated). Log saved to INC-7892 for post-mortem if needed.
- Next shift: please continue monitoring embedding p99 and kv_cache.evictions; follow up on assigned SRE-* items.

Signed off: Evan Chen (overnight on-call)
